title: A denied tool call does not fail a finished role
lead: Decide and implement what ork does when a role finishes but some of its tool calls were denied. Today the slice stops.

sections.heading: Why
sections.body: Seen 2026-10-20 in ork run ork S21 (run ork-20261020-021238-ce5a): the Haiku implementer finished its work and wrote a full report, but three side calls (mkdir, echo, shasum) were denied, and the slice stopped with 'implementer round 1 exited error'. internal/agent/claude/classify.go:20 marks any denial as denied, even on exit 0, and internal/daemon/runner.go:35-41 maps every class except ok and rate-limited to engine.ExitError. The stop reason also hides the denials: only run.json lists them. docs/state.md promises a <role>-<round>.log that the run did not write. Open design questions for the owner, to be decided before building: whether a denial stops the slice, only warns, or depends on the tool; what the stop reason and the TUI show; and whether the default allowlist should cover more (it blocks git -C, go -C, adj).

sections.heading: Failing tests
sections.body:
- A round with a success result and denied tool calls proceeds (#93); the denied tool names are recorded on the run and shown in status and the TUI.
- A denial on a round with no success result still stops the slice.
- The default implementer allowlist contains the read-only git -C, go -C and adj forms (#94).
- docs/state.md no longer promises a <role>-<round>.log (#95).

sections.heading: Implement
sections.body: Decided by the owner on 2026-10-20: #93 engine.denials (warn and continue), #94 engine.default-allowlist (add read-only forms), #95 state.role-log (drop the promise). Build them. If denials need a new wire or run-record field, stop and ask.

sections.heading: Check
sections.body:
- `go test -race ./...`, `go vet ./...`, `gofmt -l .` clean; SPDX headers; no new dependency.
- `slicer check` and `adj lint` pass.

sections.heading: Git
sections.body: One commit: "S23: a denied tool call does not fail a finished role".
